items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Leonard wrote and recorded the first three tunes on Dinah Washington’s first album, and played piano on the date.

ctx.x: Well on behalf of Hamilton College, it’s been a great, great pleasure having the poet laureate of jazz. There’s another one.

Leonard Feather. You know what we called Leonard? God rest his soul I loved him, he was a good friend of mine. But we called him “Learned Father.” Well you know why, because Leonard was the definitive jazz critic. You know most guys who play, take umbrage at being criticized — by being criticized by somebody that can’t play. Leonard wrote and recorded the first three tunes on Dinah Washington’s first album, and played piano on the date. So there you are. He has a right.

items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He composed two of the compositions and supervised Dinah Washington’s first record date.

ctx.x: He was. I had the opportunity to meet him once on a panel. I didn’t know that he was a composer.

He composed two of the compositions and supervised Dinah Washington’s first record date. He’s got good bona fides. He’s great. Leonard Feather is a real – he was truly capable of criticizing jazz music, because he could do it.
So, in 1952 you’re working in New York. Were you able to support your family at that time as a singer?
